paired_measurements.scope: Same Swift NativeJobStore, two resident processes, sequential ABBA requests; two priming calls then eight measured calls per version; not a cold-start measurement

observations: First serial App trial: GPU 4.88245 -> 4.86058 seconds; hybrid 3.01083 -> 3.01030 seconds. First native C ABI GPU trial was +1.64%; retained rather than hidden.

Later sequential trial crossed a changing machine-load interval: hybrid 3.00901 -> 3.30008 seconds; old GPU also slowed to 6.04490 seconds and new GPU to 6.01990. Browser renderer and WindowServer CPU load were observed. This does not prove a GPU utilization attribution; ABBA is the controlled follow-up.

First new App client: Core ML load 9.28946 seconds. Reversed order with a new executable name: OLD engine Core ML load 9.28632 seconds, NEW engine 0.21201 seconds. Evidence supports first-client cache preparation rather than C++ boundary overhead; no internal OS compilation trace was collected.
New-process first calls are not OS-cold-cache experiments. App benchmarks include NativeJobStore events and persistence but exclude window rendering.
Resident modes unchanged. Staged image-input mode additionally drops VAE before denoising and preserves hybrid statistics across unload. No generic block streaming or prefetch engine was introduced.

Final binary differs from the first candidate only by serializing the existing typed memory estimate directly and include ordering; final App repeats/ABBA test the packaged final binary. Regression mathematical paths and policies are unchanged.
